title: Octagons and hexagons of the Comares dado (Alhambra)

credits.source: Tiling Search, data5/J43A: Alhambra, Salón de Comares
credits.creator: Brian Wichmann
credits.note: The design was read from his line drawing; the construction (one length found by a single line from a corner of the cell) is ours.

credits.source: Photograph SPA 0204 (zellige dado of the Salón de Comares)
credits.creator: David Wade
credits.note: The real dado, used to check the wall.

given.A: Halfway from O to the next octagon.

steps.text: Rule a horizontal line through O and A and draw a circle about O through A. An octagon will sit at O and at every point two radii away along the grid.
Rule the vertical through O. At the four points where the circle meets the two lines, rule lines at right angles to them: the square cell. A small square will sit at each of its corners.

Rule the diagonal through O and the corner K, and mark where it crosses the circle. From the opposite corner of the top side, K2, rule a line through that mark: it meets the right side of the cell a little below K, at T.
Draw the circle about K through T. It meets the top of the cell at U, as far from K as T is: KT is half the diagonal of the small square at the corner. Join T and U: a side of that square.

Through U rule a vertical and through T a horizontal: the sides of the octagon and of the long hexagons. Through T and U rule lines parallel to the diagonal: the sides of the squares round the corner and the ends of the hexagons.

Where the new vertical meets the lower diagonal line, and where the new horizontal meets the upper one, are two corners of the octagon. Join them: the octagon’s slanting side, which also closes the square below the corner one.
Copy these lines to the other three corners of the cell, turning them about O.
Mark the corners of the pattern: every point where the outline of a tile turns.
The tile is the square cell.

ink.text: Ink the outline of each tile: the octagon, the halves of the long hexagons on the cell’s sides, and the squares at its corners.

pattern.text: Repeat the square cell edge to edge: octagons on the grid, a long hexagon between each two, and five small squares in a cross where four cells meet.
